text.p: Wall Street was seen opening lower on Friday after reports on the March producer price index and retail sales, analysts said.
Prices at the wholesale level fell for the third month in a row in March, the Labor Department said Friday.

But the picture was less benign when the often-volatile food and energy sector was excluded. This so-called core rate, which economists believe more closely tracks inflation, rose 0.4 percent after falling 0.1 percent in February.
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said: "I think it's a slight disappointment.
"The (retail sales number) with the revisions is a bit stronger than it looked, and the PPI, if you ex-out energy is really not particularily good, a little disappointing."
